name: tests-quarter-throttled-py-fenced-expiring-store-leases
instr:
throttled cannot elect one current owner for single-writer work or reject expired or superseded ownership. Add fenced, expiring leases with consistent behavior across synchronous and asynchronous memory, bounded-memory, and Redis stores without changing existing behavior.

Acquisition must be an atomic single-owner transition. Contention preserves the live owner. Every takeover gets a positive fencing value greater than every earlier grant for that key. Give `acquire_lease(self, key, owner, ttl)`, `inspect_lease(self, key)`, `renew_lease(self, grant, ttl)`, and `release_lease(self, grant)` equivalent outcomes across backends. Renewal extends only the matching live grant without changing fencing. Release removes only that exact grant and returns false for stale grants.

Use immutable, backend-independent public values carrying the key, owner, positive fencing value and, for states, nonnegative remaining lifetime. Before touching backend state, reject empty keys, any empty owner or nonpositive lifetime accepted by the call, and malformed or invalid grants. Report invalid input as `LeaseValidationError`, stale renewal as `LeaseOwnershipError`, and transport failures from every lease operation as `StoreUnavailableError`, preserving the original exception as the cause.

Preserve expiration, recency eviction, scalar, hash, timeout, and availability behavior. Store instances have independent lease namespaces unless a shared backend is configured; shared backends share ownership and
